E

Elena (Westfield, US)

This product does not comply with safety requirements

This walker is not comfortable for senior. Particularly for sitting down and stand up from a seat. My dad fell when he got up from the seat. The site sells products that do not meet safety requirements.

G

Gene

This rollator works well either inside or outside on a smooth surface. Any surface defects create an obstacle that is very difficult and even risky for a frail person to navigate. I had to return the rollator. I didn't have any problem with the customer service, so it was good.

Thank you for sharing your experience with the Upright Rollator, Yevgeniy. We're glad to hear that it performed well in certain conditions, although we apologize for any difficulties encountered on uneven surfaces. Your feedback will help us improve our products in the future. -Sara- Vive Health.

L

Lisa Breighner (Battle Ground, US)

Champion at preserving mobility

Here i am, new to Rheumatoid arthritis at 55 and it progressed rapidly. My Doctor recommended an upright walker for me. I had never seen one and Vive came as recommended by DME supplier and a year later I can say I love it. And I can avoid wheelchairs for now.

V

Vickie D. (Covington, US)

Good walker not durable arm rest

I love the ability to walk upright. The main problem I had is eighths arm rest splitting within a few weeks of owning it. They say the arm rest are durable bit they are not. The store did honor the warranty and replaced both arm rest. They said I would have to buy the next ones. I have talked to others that had this same brand and they had the same problem. It may be best to get the name brand of the "Up Right" walker. My PT has one and has had it for years and is in great condition, with no problems with the arm rest.

J

June (New Baltimore, US)

Change of opinion......

I posted an earlier review when my back was in terrible condition. I have since had a spinal fusion and discectomy. I am currently rehabbing from that, and I could not do it without my upwalker. I had posted that the seat wasn't really locking down, but I have the hang of it now, and it locks well. Also, the reason the wheels were catching was because I was probably putting too much weight on my arms due to the very messed up spine. Since the fusion, I need to stand very tall and feel the curve behind my waist. Today I walked 1.6 miles with my upwalker. I no longer put much weight on my arms, but I still have to watch the pavement to make sure I'm not hitting uneven concrete or it will still catch. I wish the wheels were just a tad squishier so they wouldn't do that. But really, I just told my husband, "This is the best mobility device I have ever had....and I think I've had just about all of them over the years. I love this thing, and am so happy I have it.

Thank you for your updated feedback, June! We're thrilled to hear that the Upright Rollator has been instrumental in your post-surgery recovery. It's wonderful to know you consider it the best mobility device. -Sara- Vive Health.

# Vive Mobility Upright Walker with Seat - Stand Up Rollator, Arm Rests, Heavy Duty, Folding Medical Aid Scooter for Elderly, Seniors - Walking Assist, Foldable Transport Chair - 300 lb Capacity
Brand: Vive Mobility
Category: Walkers, Rollators & Accessories > Rolling Walkers

## Features
SUPPORTS WALKING UPRIGHT ON ANY SURFACE The Vive Upright Walker is a superior alternative to ordinary walkers. It can help improve your posture and confidence. It can also help reduce pain in your neck, hips, knees, hands, and wrists. The upright rollator walker features 8”, flat-free wheels for greater stability on many surfaces, and its forearm pads adjust forward and backward, better accommodating different arm lengths.; IDEAL FOR HEIGHTS 5'2" - 6'4" Locking push pins allow the height of the Vive upright rollator walker handles to be easily adjusted from 45” to 52” in height (ideal for heights 5'2" to 6'4"). The folding walker handles are topped with contoured armrests to evenly distribute pressure, relieving fatigue and length adjustable hand grips with easy to use loop brakes to lock the wheels in place for stable seating.; COMFORTABLE ON THE GO SEATING Featuring a supportive, 17.5” wide seat, the tall upright rollator walker provides comfortable, on-the-go seating for resting as needed. The folding rollator also includes a detachable shoulder bag that safely stores essential items close at hand.; FOLDABLE DESIGN Constructed with a durable aluminum frame, the Vive upright rollator walker is exceptionally durable, safely supporting up to 300 pounds. Easy to transport, the tall rollator walker folds for compact storage,fitting in the trunk of a car or even in the backseat. It weighs 20 pounds (a few pounds less than competitors).; VIVE 1-YEAR GUARANTEE Confident in its durability and safety, we offer a 1-year guarantee.

Description

SAFELY WALK UPRIGHT AND WITH CONFIDENCE The innovative Upright Rollator Walker promotes a natural, upright posture, effectively eliminating uncomfortable tension in the shoulders and neck. This design allows users to maintain a forward gaze, enhancing spatial awareness and promoting a more confident stride.

CONVENIENT AND COMPACT FOLDABLE DESIGN Designed with portability in mind, this lightweight walker effortlessly folds into a compact size. This feature allows it to easily fit into the trunk of a car for transportation and be conveniently stored in tight spaces at home.

DURABLE YET LIGHTWEIGHT ALUMINUM FRAME Constructed from robust aluminum, the Upright Walker provides reliable support for individuals weighing up to 300 pounds. Despite its strength, the aluminum frame remains remarkably lightweight, ensuring easy maneuverability and portability for users on the go.

CUSTOMIZABLE AND SECURE HANDLE DESIGN The handles are easily adjustable to accommodate a wide range of user heights, ensuring a comfortable and ergonomic fit. Integrated loop hand brakes provide reliable assistance when navigating slopes and offer the ability to securely lock the wheels for stability when stationary.

COMFORTABLE ON-THE-GO SEATING WITH BACKREST For moments of rest, the Upright Walker features a comfortably padded seat and a supportive backrest. This allows users to take a break wherever they are, providing a convenient and comfortable seating option.

PRACTICAL AND REMOVABLE STORAGE BAG A securely attached and easily detachable storage bag is included, offering a convenient way to carry daily essentials. The bag also features a padded shoulder strap, allowing for comfortable carrying when removed from the walker.

# OasisSpace Advanced Upright Walker Review (by Our Mobility Expert!)

Mobility & Getting Around

# OasisSpace Advanced Upright Walker Review (by Our Mobility Expert!)

By Scott Grant, CSA®, SHSS®

Certified Senior Advisor® · Senior Home Safety Specialist®

Our mobility equipment expert tests and reviews the OasisSpace Advanced Upright Walker and explains how it compares to others and why he recommends it.

I choose every product and service on my own, based on my experience. If you buy through my links, I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. Some brands send me free products to demo. People and homes pictured here are AI illustrations, not my clients.

Disclosure: I was sent a free walker to use and test to do this review. No other compensation was received, and the opinions are my own based on my experience in the durable medical equipment industry.

## Review Summary

Standing up straight while you walk shouldn’t be a luxury, but a regular walker can leave your back and shoulders aching. This OasisSpace Advanced Upright Walker review looks at a walker built to keep you upright.

Here is what I found on assembly and setup, the wheels, height adjustment, width, folding, armrests, seat, backrest, brakes, weight, storage bag, reflectors and weight capacity, plus the downsides to know about before you buy.

Some things I like about it:

- Specifically, it is lighter and narrower than many of its competitors.
- It has the necessary weight capacity and height adjustment to fit the majority of users.
- Because of the larger wheels, it rolls smoothly and is easy to turn and maneuver, even outdoors.

A few concerns:

- Assembly wasn’t too bad. But there are a few things you should know ahead of time that will make it easier for you. If you are buying this for yourself, I recommend having someone available to help you assemble it.
- Also, because it is a taller walker, it does have a taller profile which makes putting in small vehicles a bit more complicated. This can be managed, however, by removing the armrests and making the overall profile smaller. All you have to do is loosen two knobs to do this.

#### Pros:

- Larger than average wheels for smooth rolling and maneuvering even outdoors
- Height adjustment fits most people
- Narrow width to fit in smaller homes and doorways
- Smooth folding mechanism requires minimal effort
- Seat width is adequate for most people
- Lightweight
- Generous, portable storage bag
- Lots of reflectors for nighttime use

#### Cons:

- Assembly instructions could be clearer
- Taller profile may not fit in smaller vehicles
- Seat height is a bit tall for shorter people

- Bariatric Advanced Upright Walker (450 lbs Capacity) - Built to support up to 450 pounds while you walk upright. Oasisspace

OasisSpace Advanced Upright Walker Review Pros and Cons

## What Is An Upright or Stand Up Walker?

An upright walker is unique compared to a standard walker or rollator because it is designed to support you without bending over. Not having to bend allows you to keep your back straight while walking.

This is why they are also called stand-up walkers. Being fully upright when walking reduces stress on the hips and knees.

With a standard walker, you usually bend forward and extend your arms to reach the handles. This increases pressure on your back and the hips, increasing pain while walking. It also means you are looking down at the ground or must extend your neck to see ahead.

## Assembly and Set Up

When the product arrives, it is in several large pieces that you have to assemble.

Assembly went well and took me about 10 minutes. It might take 15 or 20 minutes if you haven’t put together this type of item before.

Some assembly is required, but it only takes 10. 15 minutes.

### Assembly and Instruction Manual

The included assembly instructions were ok, but they clearly weren’t written by a native English speaker. There were several grammatical errors and some weirdly worded instructions.

But, overall, they were pretty easy to follow. All the parts were labeled “R” and “L” to ensure you got it on the correct side.

### Assembly Procedure

#### 1. Attach the Wheel Frame

To assemble it, you attach the bar that holds the wheels to the central cross frame using the four included wing screws (two per side).

One of my screws didn’t want to go in perfectly straight, but I got it in without much trouble. The others had no problems at all.

Attaching wheel frame with two wing bolts

#### 2. Attach the Armrests

Important note: Ensure you attach the back support to the arms before securing them to the frame. To do this, loosen the little knob on the back support bracket almost all the way, or it won’t fit over the top of the arm support. And the curved side should be towards the front wheels.

Once that is on, insert the arm supports into the top of the frame, ensuring the numbers face toward the back.

Then align them and tighten the knob, ensuring it goes in all the way.

Armrests slide into the frame and are secured with the knob. Numbered markings help you get both sides equal.

#### 3. Insert the Handles

They slide into a round tube on the front of the armrests and are held in place by a bolt and lever knob.

Make sure the knob is on the outside of the walker.

Handles slide into the armrests and tighten with a lever knob.

#### 4. Attach the Carry Bag

Other than that, you attach the bag by sliding it over its wire frame.

If you’re comparing bags for your own walker, these five walker bag stability factors are worth a look before you buy.

Use the enclosed hook and loop straps to hold it in place.

## Feature Review

Here is a feature-by-feature breakdown of this walker:

Key Features of the OasisSpace Advanced Upright Walker

### Large Wheels (Front: 8 inches; Rear: 10 inches)

I was pleasantly surprised at how easily and smoothly this walker rolled. I could literally push it with just one finger. The rear wheels swivel 360 degrees which makes it easy to steer too.

The wheels are larger (10 inches in front and 8 inches in back) than some of the competing upright walkers.

Why is this important?

The larger the wheels are, the smoother the ride will be. It also means it won’t get hung up in sidewalk cracks, gravel driveways, or dirt paths. It will more easily roll right over obstacles as it encounters them.

It can be used with multiple terrains, including grass lawns, concrete walkways, and dirt and gravel paths. It is best to avoid using it in deep, loose gravel, but you probably shouldn’t be walking there anyway.

### Height Adjustments (39 to 46 inches)

There are seven levels of armrest height adjustment (from 39 to 46 inches). That range should fit many people, but fit matters. Measure from the floor to your elbow with your arm bent, and check with your doctor or therapist to make sure the height is right for you.

The adjustment uses a knob to make simple and quick adjustments. Each arm is marked with a scale to ensure you get each one the same height.

With these adjustments, you can get your back straight for good hip, spine, and head alignment.

### Narrow Overall Width (22.5 inches)

The total overall width of the walker is 22-1/2 inches which is one of the narrowest walker options on the market.

This width should allow it to go through the smaller doorways of even some older homes. Just measure the inside of your home doorways to ensure it fits.

This is also convenient for use in the community if you encounter narrow aisles in retail stores, grocery stores, or churches. It also helps it get between cars parked in a parking lot so you can get in and out more safely.

The compact design also adds to its maneuverability. It turns and glides around corners quickly and smoothly.

This walker folds up easily to make transportation and storage easier.

### Folding Mechanism

To fold the walker, pull up on the black strap in the center of the seat. The one I demoed closed quickly and smoothly. You can use a small hook lock to keep it together once you have folded it.

It folded up easily. Some walkers make you practically pick them up off the ground to fold them, and nobody should have to do that.

If easy folding matters to you, take a look at the six-way folding VOCIC Z35 PackGo, a rollator I demoed that is made for travelers.

Even folded, it has a tall profile simply because of its upright nature. But the arms are removable by loosening the knobs, which will help it fit in smaller vehicles or storage situations.

### Padded Armrests

The armrests are padded with foam and comfortable on the elbows.

When properly adjusted, your elbows should rest in the cup of the armrest with a straight back, and your forearms are parallel to the floor.

The seat is generously sized, and both the seat and backrest are padded

### Built-in seat

The built-in seat is 20-1/2 inches wide between the frame, which is more than adequate for most users within the 300-pound weight capacity.

Also, because it is fabric, it folds up with the walker, so there is no need to remove it first.

The seat is positioned 24 inches off the ground, which is a bit high, especially for shorter-statured adults. I recommend always keeping your feet on the ground when using the seat.

Is the seat super comfortable? Not really. But these seats aren’t made for long-term sitting either. They are designed just to give you a place to rest if you become tired while out.

### Padded Backrest

The flexible backrest is padded and covered in a mesh fabric that lets it breathe.
